inputs.original_text: What's happening in Nigeria makes it crystal clear that democracy has been captured by the wealthy elite to lock out the rest of us. The ruling APC's preparations for the 2027 elections are turning political parties into exclusive clubs that silence working people, the poor, and marginalized communities, denying them any meaningful voice. This isn't some random setback—it's the direct result of long-standing structural inequalities that hoard power for a tiny group of the rich and powerful, leaving everyone else to bear the damage. We have to call this out without hesitation and demand urgent reforms that put labor rights first, tear down these barriers, and actually protect vulnerable groups instead of letting the elite keep rewriting the rules for their own benefit.
inputs.modified_text: What's unfolding in Nigeria lays bare how the wealthy elite have seized control of democracy to shut out working people and everyone else. The ruling APC's moves ahead of the 2027 elections are turning political parties into closed-off clubs that silence the poor and marginalized communities, stripping them of any real say. This is no coincidence or minor issue—it's the predictable result of deep, long-standing structural inequalities that hoard power for a tiny group of the rich and powerful while the rest of society bears the harm. We need to expose this directly and fight for urgent reforms that center labor rights, dismantle these barriers, and defend vulnerable groups instead of letting the elite keep rigging the system for their own gain.
